aliases.name: Orange Soda story
aliases.meaning: after the original Creepypasta Wiki author handle

description.summary: A widely-shared internet horror story, posted to the Creepypasta Wiki on 10 August 2010, framed as a declassified record of a Soviet experiment in which prisoners kept awake for 15 days by a stimulant gas descend into psychotic violence. It is fiction; investigations by Snopes and others have repeatedly confirmed there is no such Soviet experiment.
description.full: 'The Russian Sleep Experiment' is one of the most-shared horror creepypastas of the early internet era. Originally posted on 10 August 2010 to the Creepypasta Wiki by a user with the handle 'OrangeSoda', the story claims to be a leaked record of a Soviet research project conducted between 1940 and 1951 in which five political prisoners are kept awake for fifteen days by a stimulant gas, sealed in a chamber and observed via microphone and one-way glass. The text describes the subjects' progressive psychosis, paranoid hallucinations, refusal to be allowed to sleep, self-mutilation, evisceration, and apparent transformation into superhumanly strong, near-immortal creatures. The story circulated on Reddit, YouTube narrations, Tumblr and link-aggregators, and is widely re-shared as if it were a genuine Soviet record. It is, however, fiction: there is no archival or scientific evidence of such an experiment, and Snopes, news.com.au, LiveAbout and the Creepypasta Wiki itself classify it as fabricated. The story has nonetheless been hugely influential, generating multiple novels and at least two feature-film adaptations and serving as a paradigm case of mistaken-for-true internet folklore in academic discussions of digital legend.

etymology.origin: Internet horror-fiction subculture (creepypasta), originally on the Creepypasta Wiki
etymology.meaning: 'Creepypasta' is a portmanteau of 'creepy' + 'copypasta' (text copy-pasted across forums); 'Russian Sleep Experiment' is descriptive of the framing.

features.description: Five Soviet political prisoners locked in a sealed gas-chamber laboratory under microphone and one-way-glass observation
An unnamed experimental gas claimed to prevent sleep for the duration of the test
Subjects are described as tearing their own flesh, drinking blood, and removing organs while remaining alive
By the end of the story the subjects exhibit superhuman strength and refuse anaesthetic that does not result in renewed sleep

physical.morphology: Within the fiction, the subjects are ordinary humans who undergo radical psychological and physiological deterioration; no consistent monster anatomy is given outside that narrative.

abilities.description: Central premise: the experimental gas keeps subjects continuously awake for fifteen days
Subjects in the story display strength far beyond human norms by the end of the experiment

range.description: Internet-native phenomenon: originated on the Creepypasta Wiki and spread through English-language forums, Reddit, YouTube and Tumblr; subsequently translated into many languages.

hotspots.name: Creepypasta Wiki

location.description: Original publication site (Wikidot, later Fandom) for the story

hotspots.notes: Hosts the canonical text and edit history of the story

first_recorded.source: Creepypasta Wiki edit history; Snopes 2019 fact-check

peak_activity_periods.description: Mass virality on YouTube horror narration channels and Reddit; entrenchment as one of the canonical creepypastas

origins.cultural_roots: Late-2000s creepypasta subculture, which adapted earlier horror chain-emails and 4chan posts into a sustained collaborative literary form.
origins.earliest_accounts: First posted to the Creepypasta Wiki on 10 August 2010 by a user with the handle 'OrangeSoda'; the underlying author's identity is not publicly verified.
origins.folklore_connections: Builds on Cold-War conspiracy folklore (MKULTRA, Philadelphia Experiment, secret Soviet science) and on the older horror trope of the experiment-gone-wrong.

timeline.event: User 'OrangeSoda' posts 'The Russian Sleep Experiment' on the Creepypasta Wiki
Story spreads on YouTube horror narration channels with millions of cumulative views
timeline.significance: Peak viral phase; many viewers begin sharing it as a genuine Soviet record

timeline.event: Snopes publishes fact-check confirming the story is fiction
Feature film adaptation 'The Soviet Sleep Experiment' (dir. Barry Andersson) is released, starring Chris Kattan

history.modern_era: The Russian Sleep Experiment is now a standard reference case in academic discussions of digital legend and creepypasta. It is also a reliable test case for media-literacy programmes because its 'declassified-document' framing continues to convince first-time readers despite long-standing debunkings.

location.description: Creepypasta Wiki (Wikidot), an internet horror-fiction site

notable.description: User 'OrangeSoda' posts the text of 'The Russian Sleep Experiment' on the Creepypasta Wiki. The story claims to describe a Soviet experiment in which five prisoners are kept awake for 15 days by a stimulant gas and descend into psychosis and self-mutilation. The post is the canonical origin of the creepypasta.

factors: Wiki edit history is independently verifiable
credibility.notes: The 'event' here is the publication of the fiction, not any real experiment.

documentary.name: Original Creepypasta Wiki entry

documentary.analysis: Verified as the originating text by Snopes and by independent inspection of the wiki's revision history.

documentary.name: Snopes fact-check (2019)
documentary.description: Snopes article assessing the story; rated as fiction with no real-world Soviet referent.
documentary.analysis: One of the key authoritative debunkings cited by news outlets and academics.

scientific.name: Sleep deprivation does not produce the effects described
scientific.description: Real-world sleep-deprivation research (e.g. the 1964 Randy Gardner case at 264 hours awake, and laboratory studies in healthy volunteers) produces cognitive impairment, microsleeps, and transient psychotic-like symptoms, but no observed self-evisceration, transformation, or sustained superhuman strength.
evidence_cited: Absence of any peer-reviewed report of the alleged Soviet experiment

skeptical.name: Internet creepypasta
skeptical.description: The Russian Sleep Experiment is a faux-document horror fiction posted to the Creepypasta Wiki in 2010. There is no archival, journalistic, or scientific evidence of any such Soviet experiment.
evidence_cited: Absence of corroborating Soviet archival material
Author handle 'OrangeSoda' identified in the wiki history

stories: YouTube horror narration adaptations (e.g. CreepsMcPasta, MrCreepyPasta)
folklore.beliefs: Frequently mistaken for a genuine Soviet record by casual readers; treated by online horror communities as a canonical fictional reference.
